source.title: Hybrid Optimizer Switching for Deep Neural Network Training in Time Series Forecasting

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The paper metadata says Vol. 2024, No. 1, November 2024, while the supplied ID and venue year indicate 2026; no resolution is stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares optimizer test performance on M4 time-series forecasting, an extension beyond the image-classification and language-model settings in V4. It does not report training performance, so it cannot assess the training-to-test comparison in that version.
record.gate_note: Table I reports test accuracy and minimum test loss by optimizer and learning rate. The paper also reports loss ranges in Table II. It does not test random-label memorization, width, convolutional architecture, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out performance of an LSTM trained with Adam, momentum SGD, and Adam-to-SGD switching on M4 Weekly forecasting. These results test V4's optimizer comparison and switching mechanism in a new workload, outside its stated image and language benchmarks.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' statements: the discussion favors Adam overall and notes a small hybrid advantage at 0.002, while the conclusion promotes the hybrid as achieving competitive accuracy, lower test loss, and more stable convergence. That general conclusion exceeds Table I: the hybrid beats Adam only at 0.002, and its Table II loss range is the largest.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares Adam, SGD with momentum, and a hybrid using Adam for the first 80% of training then SGD with momentum; it evaluates M4 time-series forecasting rather than the benchmark settings in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: Test performance varies with learning rate; the hybrid slightly exceeds Adam at 0.002, while Adam leads at the other reported learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Reported loss ranges are 0.0096 for Adam, 0.0021 for SGD, and 0.0457 for the hybrid.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizers differ in loss variation across the reported learning-rate settings; these ranges alone do not establish generalization or convergence stability.

record.peer_reviewed: Anusandhanvallari, Vol 2024, No. 1 (venue/year conflict with provided year 2026)
record.problems: Only one dataset and an LSTM forecasting setup are described. Model size, training accuracy, and train-to-test gaps are not reported. No uncertainty estimates or controls are stated. The reported accuracy values include very low values for SGD, but the text does not define the accuracy calculation or report a chance baseline.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported Table I optimizer-by-learning-rate results were left out. Table II loss range values are included as R16–R18. Figure 2 and Figure 4 are described qualitatively, but add no distinct numeric measure relevant to V4.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Image and language benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; systematic tuning of decay schedules or broader hyperparameters; decoupled weight decay; word-level language models.
Batch-size effects under fixed or adapted epoch budgets.
Dropout, training-set size, and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, generalization gaps, and rankings against alternative measures.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: All Table I values match the supplied text. Forecasting accuracy lacks a reproducible definition, training performance and uncertainty are unreported, and minimum test loss is an extremum rather than a clearly specified final-checkpoint score. The learning-rate search is shared and narrow; optimizer-specific tuning and equal training budgets are insufficiently documented. Because V4 states a tendency on image and language benchmarks, the forecasting reversal limits its extension rather than directly refuting that stated tendency.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Image-classification and language benchmarks; training-performance comparisons; broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching as a recovery method, and word-level language models.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy changes.

relationships.condition: Adam versus momentum SGD on M4 Weekly forecasting at all five reported learning rates.
relationships.reason: R1–R2, R4–R5, R7–R8, R10–R11, and R13–R14 favor Adam on both test metrics; the adaptive-method disadvantage does not extend to this forecasting setup.
relationships.display_finding: Reported Adam advantages over momentum SGD on both test metrics across all five learning rates remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Adam-to-SGD switching at learning rate 0.002 on M4 Weekly forecasting.
relationships.reason: R9 shows only a small switching benefit over Adam: accuracy 72.48% versus 72.24% and minimum test loss 0.2752 versus 0.2776, without uncertainty estimates.
relationships.display_finding: Reported small accuracy and minimum-test-loss improvements over Adam remain unverified and lack uncertainty estimates.

relationships.condition: Adam-to-SGD switching at learning rates 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001, and 0.0005 on M4 Weekly forecasting.
relationships.reason: R3, R6, R12, and R15 show lower accuracy and higher minimum test loss than Adam; switching's benefit depends on the learning rate in this setup.
relationships.display_finding: Reported lower accuracy and higher minimum test loss after switching remain unverified.

reader_labels.condition: M4 time-series forecasting at learning rate 0.002; Adam compared with the hybrid optimizer
reader_labels.reason: The hybrid optimizer, which switches from Adam to SGD, slightly exceeds Adam on both reported test metrics at this one learning rate (R7, R9); other tested rates favor Adam over the hybrid (R1, R3, R4, R6, R10, R12, R13, R15).
